blurb: A declaration or member has one doc. Two doc lines in a row are two docs, not one of two lines. For more than one line, write a doc block: a `---` line, the text, and another `---` line. When every doc is a one-line `--- text`, the fix that joins them into a block is machine-applicable, so `bynk check --fix` applies it.
example:
--- Doubles a number.
--- Used by the pricing code.          // ✗ a second doc
fn double(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }

---                                    // ✓ one doc block
Doubles a number.
Used by the pricing code.
---
fn double(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }
summary: A declaration or member has two docs directly above it; a target has one doc, so a doc of more than one line is a `---` block.
